solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the blog titled it No 2048, which the sequence puts at 2408

clue.text: Tory secretary's out of office — in study

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a temp is a temporary secretary
late means former, as in 'the late chairman', no longer holding office

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's assistant has left the office and is now studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of office' looks like the secretary's away message, but it gives LATE in the sense of 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something closely is to ponder or consider it at length; both are verbs.

clue.text: Needlecraft, note, lacking the more elevated 'ton'

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so one letter is taken out of the note

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note
T is the abbreviation for ton; the note has two Ts and in a down entry the higher one is the first

explanation.surface: A sewing hobby described with a fussy remark about a missing high tone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer letters stack vertically, so 'more elevated' picks the upper of the two Ts in the note.
explanation.definitionFit: Crochet is a craft of looping yarn with a hooked needle, so it counts as needlecraft.

clue.text: Adults only allowed in nick?

indicators.note: allowed in says the grid word is to be read as an entry notice saying who may come through the door

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for children; split three and two, the grid word reads as a ban on them, so only grown-ups may come

explanation.surface: A sign on a bar or club door saying only grown-ups may enter.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split 3,2 the answer reads NOT CH, children barred, which is what 'Adults only' means. 'Nick' looks like prison slang tying in with 'allowed in', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or groove, the same as a notch in wood.

clue.text: Weakness in view — watch strap almost through

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite finished, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before the cut
in can mean through, as in coming in the window

explanation.surface: A watch strap worn almost through, described as a weak point in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' and 'strap' look like one object, a wristwatch band, but watch is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, sore eyes after long reading or screen use are a weakness of sight.

clue.text: Petition peer about marina's closing

indicators.note: about means going round, so the snooping word wraps the letter

parts.note: to pry is to peer nosily

indicators.note: closing points to the final letter of marina's

explanation.surface: Someone appealing to a lord concerning the end of a marina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' suggests a lord, but it is the verb meaning look closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition is to make an earnest request, as one does to God or a court.

clue.text: Arms and legs but no running needed on the pitch!

definitions.meaning: on hands and knees, crawling like a four-legged animal

definitions.text: no running needed on the pitch!
definitions.meaning: in cricket a ball hit to the boundary scores four runs without the batters running, so a batter hitting only these needs no running

explanation.surface: A sporting joke about limbs and a lazy afternoon at the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball reaching the boundary along the ground scores four automatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down on hands and knees uses all four limbs at once, while boundary hits score four each.

clue.text: Crew's perfection hard to ignore

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave out, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: the height of something is its peak or perfection, as in 'the height of fashion'
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A boat crew's flawless performance is hard to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to ignore' reads as a phrase meaning conspicuous, but it is split: hard gives H, and 'to ignore' drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a racing boat and its team of eight oarsmen.

clue.text: After about nineteen weeks maiden tried perversely to get married

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: perversely means wrongly or contrarily, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman tries awkwardly to get wed after a long engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the midpoint of a pregnancy, roughly twenty weeks, as well as the middle of a school term.
explanation.definitionFit: Halfway through a forty-week pregnancy falls at about nineteen or twenty weeks, the middle of the term.

clue.text: Charmer from south unsettled and mischievous at heart

parts.note: a moot point is one still open to debate, unsettled

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letters of the word mischievous

explanation.surface: A smooth-talker from the south, unpredictable and naughty underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave, ingratiating man is a charmer, often one who is a little too slick.

clue.text: Precisely where to paint?

definitions.meaning: exactly right, as in paying bang on time
nail varnish is painted on the fingernail

explanation.surface: A decorator asking exactly where to apply the paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for exactly, at once, and literally the spot where nail polish goes.

clue.text: Took a chance, rampaged about, avoiding rap

indicators.note: about means turned around or jumbled, so the letters are mixed up
avoiding means the letters of rap are left out of the mixture

explanation.surface: A gambler ran wild but dodged the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of RAP out of RAMPAGED and rearrange the remaining AMGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To game is to gamble, so gamed is the past tense of taking a chance on a bet.

clue.text: Bit of a laugh separating socks — they clash

indicators.note: separating means coming between, so the laugh splits the punching word

parts.note: socks as a verb means punches, hits
ha is one burst of laughter, part of ha-ha

explanation.surface: A joke splitting up pairs of socks with clashing colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'socks' and 'clash' suggest clashing patterns, but socks is the verb meaning hits.
explanation.definitionFit: These paired cymbals on a drum kit are struck together by a foot pedal.

clue.text: Refuge offered by nut?

parts.note: a hiding place, cryptically the opening a bolt goes through before a nut is screwed on

explanation.surface: A shelter provided by a crazy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' suggests an eccentric, but here it is the metal fastener that pairs with a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway to escape to, and literally the hole through which a threaded fastener passes.

clue.text: On the radio, unreasonably reject winger

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the words are spoken

parts.note: too means excessively, beyond what is reasonable, and to can is to throw out

explanation.surface: A broadcaster unfairly dismisses a football winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' looks like a footballer, but it is a creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird with a huge bright beak is a winged creature, so a winger in crossword terms.

clue.text: Enfeebled, like an empty 6?

definitions.meaning: made weak, robbed of strength and vigour
6 is the rowing crew of eight; a boat with no crew has nobody aboard

explanation.surface: A weakened state compared with an abandoned boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnerved or weakened in spirit, and literally lacking any crew aboard.

clue.text: Brahms regularly entertaining ill-mannered coach

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the picked letters go round the rude word
regularly picks every other letter of the composer's name

parts.note: rough can mean crude or ill-mannered

explanation.surface: The composer playing host to a rude sports coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a trainer, but it is the horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a type of coach.

clue.text: Depression acquired at birth?

parts.note: a hollow in the belly left when the cord is cut at birth, not a mood

explanation.surface: A question about mental low spirits present from birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood, but it is a dip in the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel is a small hollow in the abdomen formed when the umbilical cord falls away.

clue.text: Restlessness shown by Ms Rykiel engaging medium

parts.note: by can mean in, as in 'by day' meaning in the day

indicators.note: engaging means taking on or holding, so the designer's name holds the letter

parts.note: Sonia Rykiel was a French fashion designer
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's sleepless nights shown in her medium-sized range.
explanation.definitionFit: Inability to sleep leaves a person tossing and turning, a state of restlessness at night.

clue.text: Back road beside quarry — deserted narrowboat just round the corner

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the road's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written here with I for the 1
a mine is a pit where minerals are dug, like a quarry

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, so only the outer letters of narrowboat stay

explanation.surface: Directions to a canal boat abandoned by a quarry off a back road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen any moment is coming soon, figuratively near at hand.

clue.text: Find fault with the setter's cracker

parts.note: the setter is 'I', so the setter's is I'm, I am
a cracker is something excellent, as is a peach

explanation.surface: Criticising the puzzle-maker's Christmas cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracker' suggests a party novelty or biscuit, but it means a great one, as does peach.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to accuse or call into question, so to criticise or challenge.

clue.text: A black queen can be superior

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Bess is a familiar name for Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A dark chess queen proving the stronger piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' is the noun, as in mother superior, the head of a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns is its mother superior.

clue.text: Female concealing passion for guard

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the pronoun wraps round the passion word

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
heat is intense passion, as in 'the heat of the moment'

explanation.surface: A woman hiding her ardour for a security guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guard' is a verb here: to cover a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a sword in its scabbard is to cover and protect it, a way to guard its blade.

clue.text: Possible crisis averted from container ships toppling monument

indicators.note: possible means the word crisis may appear in any order among the letters
averted from means turned away out of the larger phrase, so those letters are removed
toppling means falling over, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A disaster narrowly avoided when container vessels nearly fell onto a landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, R, I, S, I, S from CONTAINERSHIPS and rearrange the leftover ONTANEHP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panthéon in Paris is a monumental building housing the tombs of great French citizens.

clue.text: In truth, it checks progress?

indicators.note: in means the word lies inside the run of letters across truth, it and checks

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark that honesty slows things down.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or obstacle holds up or interrupts the flow of events.

clue.text: Scratches heard in writer's passage?

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to claw is to scratch, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Scratching noises audible in an author's corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' suggests a hallway, but it is a section of text.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a written document, a contract or a sentence, is a passage of text.

clue.text: Mouth part starts to ululate vocals — ukulele lead's awesome

indicators.note: starts to points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A singer warbling to an excellent ukulele accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lobe hanging at the back of the soft palate is a part of the mouth.

clue.text: Venetian knave — one in the past

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ago means before now, in the past

explanation.surface: A rogue from Venice belonging to an earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello, the villainous ensign is a scheming Venetian rogue.

clue.text: Strip purple vehicle

indicators.note: strip means peel off the outside, so the colour loses its first and last letters

parts.note: magenta is a purplish-red colour

explanation.surface: Peel off a car's purple paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' looks like a car, but it means a means or medium, as in a vehicle for change.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle can be a channel through which something is done, as an agent is a means or instrument.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing keeping his money under the bed?

definitions.text: keeping his money under the bed?
definitions.meaning: someone stashing cash under the mattress has no bank facility

explanation.surface: A wastrel who hides his savings under the mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthless person is a wastrel, and literally someone without any bank.

clue.text: S-Sovereign?

parts.note: the first letter of the word state is S

explanation.surface: A stammered royal title.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is the trick: the first S is the start of the word state.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the ceremonial ruler and chief representative of a nation.
